claims.statement: For full-size P-256 input Q=[x]P, the algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed H1, M1/L-ori, H3 and H-trail premises. The total classical work is at most 2^126.73175 units at C=1000. The negation-class rho attack uses A=2^27 adders, K=2^32 walks, batches of 2^20, the prior three-arm schedule and thirty-two-copy forward and backward loops. Each backward entry uses a five-bit dispatch. Long-range anchor-cap branch uses a local test and unconditional trampoline; rare exits and re-entry cost are charged. Computation includes correction metering, preprocessing, failures, transfers, lookup, replay and verification. Memory is below 2^77 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^84.961190 and included; no advice. This is an analytic conditional claim, not a full-scale execution. H1 posits the collision law with its small-key table extension; M1/L-ori posit conditional fresh-class exposure and pseudorandom keys; H3 prices the stated instruction paths; H-trail bounds average correction work per fresh trail, with the stated dy fold model. Adders satisfy 2^192 <= x < 2^231 and the y-window in proof.md; the distinguished test is x < 2^196. The statistical and cost premises, stopping rules, full resource accounting and evidence are in proof.md and probability.md.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the revised full production cost ledger (including the correction charge, its meter slack and abort term) and order certificate, then run the inherited complete reduced-order procedure, with checkpoint-only cycle detection and the small-key adder key rule at toy scale (adder_key_shift 2: adders redrawn until key < p>>2; shift 4 exceeded the runner's time limit; no y window), at tau=0.4943, the production value on its 0.0001 grid, retaining failures and replay checks. The two results have distinct scopes; neither establishes production mixing.

title: P-256 sigma rho: sixteen-copy blocks on the three-arm anchor schedule
